name: AesCode-8B and AesCode-32B (Microsoft)
purpose: Microsoft states: generate information-rich visual artifacts (slides, posters, dashboards, reports) as structured, editable HTML/CSS, using an image generated from the same prompt as an aesthetic reference while following the prompt for the content; also research on multimodal code generation and verifiable visual design.

lineage.how_derived: cold-start SFT then GDPO reinforcement learning with seven decoupled cross-modal reward channels and graph-structured supervision

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card, "following the Qwen3-VL backbone")
license.notes: Card tag and License section say Apache 2.0; neither repository has a LICENSE file (checked 2026-11-19), so the text was not read.

architecture.why_this_design: The card reasons about the training design, not the architecture: separating semantic requirements from visual cues through graph-structured supervision and decoupled cross-modal rewards, because off-the-shelf VLMs copy hallucinated content from the reference or ignore its layout. The 32B entry here is the large size; the 8B has the same recipe.

engine_support.notes: GGUFs and mmproj files exist (bartowski, prithivMLmods).

benchmarks.name: Infographic Overall (300 samples, with image reference), AesCode-32B
Infographic Overall (300 samples, with image reference), AesCode-8B

strengths: Vendor table: AesCode-8B Overall 82.94 and AesCode-32B 85.89 on 300 infographic samples, above reference-conditioned GPT-5.5 (81.28) and Claude Opus 4.8 (80.39)
weaknesses: Narrow purpose: HTML/CSS infographics, not software engineering
Style score is the shared ceiling (about 53 to 58 for every system)
vendor numbers only; needs an image-generator reference for its best results
best_for: generating slides, posters and dashboards as editable HTML
avoid_for: coding agents, code review, general programming
soft.maturity: Microsoft research release with a paper (arXiv 2610.18860) and project page; 2k downloads per repo.

tona_fit.reason: Not a software-engineering model: a document/visual-design generator. It fits a document or presentation role (see the documents area) rather than the coding worker; 8B at 5.2 GB (Q4_K_M) runs on every PC class and the 32B at 20.5 GB on 16 GB with streaming, both estimated.
blockers: needs a reference image generator for best results

open_questions: Evaluation of its HTML output by our own harness (the vendor judges with its own checklist). Check: a small render-and-judge test.
Per-language quality: no public per-language numbers found. Check: our own polyglot run per language.
